title: Data residency & export-control redline scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal reference for clauses to watch and pragmatic redlines when customers push back on data residency, cross-border transfer, and export-control language for Private/Dedicated deployments. Keep short, prioritized, and playbook-oriented so can paste into replies or negotiation notes.

1) Core issues to flag early:
- Scope of covered data: "personal data" vs "customer data" vs "customer confidential info". Narrow it to customer-provided content and logs that include PII; exclude aggregated/anonymous telemetry.
- Residency promise: absolute (data stored only in X) vs best-efforts vs residency for "backup/replica". Prefer: primary processing and storage in region X; backups may be stored encrypted in region Y with notice.
- Export-control carveouts: encryption, access by support engineers, and lawful interception. If they demand explicit export restrictions, ask for a technical definition and cite impacted infra (CDNs, monitoring, OS patches).
- KMS / key control: customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) acceptable for Private, but need clear ops-run exceptions for emergency access and patching.

2) Suggested redlines (concise snippets to propose)
- Data scope: "Customer Data means data, content, and metadata provided or uploaded by Customer in connection with the Services; does not include aggregated/anonymized usage metrics or Model weights."
- Residency: "Provider will at all times store and process Customer Data for production workloads in Region(s): [X]. Backups or passive replicas may be stored in [X, Y] provided they are encrypted at rest with keys controlled by Provider and Customer is notified."
- Cross-border transfers: "Provider may transfer Customer Data where required for legal compliance or to operate services; Provider will rely on standard contractual clauses or equivalent safeguards and notify Customer where feasible."
- KMS: "If Customer elects CMK, Provider will use keys only for encryption at rest. Provider will not export plaintext. Emergency access requires Customer approval except in narrowly defined platform-recovery scenarios (log + post-incident notice)."

3) Prioritization ladder (what we will fight for vs concede)
- Fight for: narrow definition of data scope; ability to use aggregated telemetry; reasonable residency language (not absolute global ban); ability to use provider-side ops for patching with audit trail.
- Concede: limited geographic replication for durability; controller/processor label tweaks; limited audit access via redacted reports rather than full access.

4) Liability & remedies quick heuristics
- Avoid unlimited carveouts tied to residency breach. Tie damages to standard cap language except for proven willful misconduct or gross negligence tied to export violations with regulatory fines.
- If they insist on regulatory fines carveout for export control (rare), ask for: (a) caps still apply, (b) mutual indemnity for government penalties resulting from Customer misconfiguration.

5) Questions to surface on the call (to ops/product before promising anything)
- Can infra guarantee phys location for live KV stores? Which cloud regions (azs) are sticky?
- Backup retention & replication topology (CDN, object-store cross-region replication?)
- Support/Debug access: what logs contain plaintext? Can we provide redacted logs?
- KMS options: CMK supported? HSM? Latency and availability implications?

6) Quick negotiation scripts (one-liners to paste into email)
- If they ask for "no cross-border transfers": "We can commit production storage in Region X and use encryption and SCCs for necessary transfers; absolute bans on all transfers would prevent us from offering managed support and automatic failover—can we agree on a narrowly scoped exception for platform resilience?"
- If they ask for full audit rights: "We can provide a scoped audit or a SOC2/ISO report plus targeted evidence; full remote access to provider infra is a non-starter from a security and multi-tenant compliance perspective."

7) Fall-back positions & escalation triggers
- If legal insists on absolute residency, escalate to product: options are Dedicated single-tenant in-customer VPC or Private on-prem bundle (cost/lead time estimate).
- If they demand KMS with no provider access at all, escalate to infra & SRE for risk assessment; may require custom ops playbooks and higher pricing.

8) Examples of bad customer language to counter quickly
- "Provider will not transfer Customer Data outside of [COUNTRY] under any circumstances." -> counter with resilience/patching risks + propose narrow exception list.
- "Provider shall provide full remote access and extractable backups to Customer on demand." -> counter with security/multi-tenant risk; offer redacted exports or export under third-party escrow.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Draft a one-page tech appendix for sales explaining replication/backups/KMS options and costs to attach to NDAs.
- Run a short internal Q/A session with SRE (Riley) to confirm what we actually can guarantee for Private deployments.
- Update contract-template branch with standard residency clause and CMK option (PR ref above).

End of scratchpad. Keep updated as field cases come in.
